Imagine the wind never stopped.
Not for an hour.
Not for a day.
Not ever.
And every hour, it would grow a little stronger.
At first, you would hardly notice.
Twenty kilometers per hour.
A few leaves tumbling down the street.
The palm trees would sway gently, the way they always do.
Just a pleasant, breezy morning.
Nobody would think twice about it.
By fifty, something would start to feel wrong.
Paper would race along the pavement.
Leaves would whirl up between the buildings.
Walking into it would take real effort.
Shop signs would rattle and swing on their hooks.
Seventy.
The café chairs would start to slide, then tumble down the road.
Every tree on the avenue would bend and roar.
The wind would howl between the buildings, a sound that never fades.
At ninety, this would be a full storm.
People would hurry indoors.
Drivers would pull over and wait.
Then even the heavy bins would start to roll.
One hundred and twenty.
Hurricane force.
The wind would roar like a passing train.
Except this train would never pass.
A real hurricane would pass within a day or two.
This one never would.
